boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented ECU rituals, campus legends and recurring celebrations, including one tradition that concluded in 2026.

cards.title: Wait Until Graduation to Walk Under the Cupola
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Mall
cards.notes: Pause at the Cupola for a photo, then take the surrounding paths until graduation if you want to follow ECU’s four-year superstition.
cards.short_summary: A campus legend says passing beneath the Cupola before graduating delays a four-year graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU describes the Cupola as a campus tradition and says legend holds that students who walk under it before graduating will not graduate in four years.
cards.source_title: Rich with Tradition | Undergraduate Admissions | ECU
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark on the Main Campus Mall; follow campus access guidance.

cards.title: Make the No Quarter Cross in the Fourth
cards.subtitle: ECU athletic events
cards.notes: At an ECU game, watch for the fourth-quarter No Quarter moment and join the approved crowd gesture only when the game presentation cues it.
cards.short_summary: The red No Quarter flag and crossed-arm gesture signal ECU’s late-game Pirate identity.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU states that, when entering the fourth quarter, students raise their arms in a cross and cheer ECU teams onward to victory as part of No Quarter.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during athletic events; game admission or ticket requirements may apply.

cards.title: Ring In, Then Ring Out
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Student Center entrance
cards.notes: Find the Boneyard Bell by the Main Campus Student Center entrance and ring it at an arrival or graduation milestone, as its plaque invites.
cards.short_summary: SGA’s recommissioned bell marks the beginning and ending of a student’s ECU journey.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU SGA says incoming students ring the Boneyard Bell when they arrive and graduating students ring it as they leave their alma mater.
cards.source_title: Boneyard Bell | Student Government Association | ECU
cards.access_notes: Located at the main entrance of the Main Campus Student Center; observe any event or building access rules.

cards.title: Close Spring Classes at Barefoot on the Mall
cards.subtitle: ECU Mall
cards.notes: Check the Student Activities Board’s spring programming and attend the Mall celebration on the final day of classes before exams begin.
cards.short_summary: Since 1979, ECU has used this annual event to mark the end of spring-semester classes.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU reports that Barefoot on the Mall began in 1979, is held on the last day of spring classes, and is hosted annually by the Student Activities Board.
cards.source_title: Barefoot on the Mall celebrates end of academic year | News Services | ECU
cards.access_notes: Annual spring-semester event; consult ECU’s current event details for attendance information.

cards.title: Remember the Polar Bear Plunge
cards.subtitle: Eakin Student Recreation Center outdoor pool
cards.notes: Treat this as ECU history: the 30th and final plunge was scheduled for January 2026, closing a tradition that began in 1997.
cards.short_summary: A cold-weather pool-jump tradition ran for 30 years before ECU announced its final event.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU reported that the 30th and final Polar Bear Plunge was planned for January 2026 and that the first event occurred in January 1997.
cards.source_title: Final Polar Bear Plunge reflects campus tradition | News Services | ECU
cards.access_notes: Discontinued after its final 2026 event; do not attempt an unsupervised pool jump.

cards.title: Start the Year at Pirate Palooza
cards.subtitle: Pirate Weeks of Welcome
cards.notes: Look for Pirate Palooza in the fall welcome schedule and use it to sample activities, games and campus organizations with new classmates.
cards.short_summary: ECU’s large welcome-back gathering is part of the opening rhythm of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU News Services identifies Pirate Palooza as an ECU tradition and ECU’s largest welcome-back event.
cards.access_notes: Typically associated with fall welcome programming; verify the current year’s schedule and location.

cards.title: Answer “Purple!” With “Gold!”
cards.subtitle: ECU campus and athletic culture
cards.notes: Learn the short Purple–Gold call-and-response during orientation, then use it when it is led at ECU gatherings or athletic events.
cards.short_summary: The school-color chant is introduced to new Pirates as part of ECU campus culture.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU’s orientation guidance tells incoming students to learn the “Purple! Gold!” chant as part of campus culture.
cards.access_notes: Used at university gatherings and games; participate when led by event staff or performers.

cards.title: Learn “E.C. Victory” Before Game Day
cards.subtitle: ECU athletic events
cards.notes: Read the official lyrics before a game and follow the band, cheer squad or videoboard so you can join the song at the right time.
cards.short_summary: ECU identifies its fight song as an essential Pirate tradition to learn.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU’s admissions tradition guide names “E.C. Victory” as the university fight song and calls the fight song essential to learn.
cards.source_title: Rich with Tradition | Undergraduate Admissions | ECU
cards.access_notes: Commonly heard at athletic events; game admission or ticket requirements may apply.

cards.title: Keep the Alma Mater in the Rotation
cards.subtitle: University ceremonies and ECU gatherings
cards.notes: Save the official Alma Mater lyrics and listen for it at ECU ceremonies or gatherings, where it connects current students with alumni.
cards.short_summary: The Alma Mater is one of the songs ECU explicitly asks Pirates to know.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU’s admissions tradition guide presents the East Carolina University Alma Mater and calls the alma mater essential to learn.
cards.source_title: Rich with Tradition | Undergraduate Admissions | ECU
cards.access_notes: Ceremonial use varies by event; follow the program and event staff directions.

cards.title: Spot the Trustees Mace at Commencement
cards.subtitle: ECU graduation ceremonies
cards.notes: At commencement, look for the handcrafted Trustees Mace in the formal procession and read its history as part of ECU’s ceremonial tradition.
cards.short_summary: A specially commissioned ceremonial mace became an early symbolic tradition at ECU.
cards.evidence_claim: ECU News Services reports that the Trustees Mace was commissioned before the 1978 chancellor installation and was among ECU’s first symbolic traditions.
cards.source_title: ECU uses ancient symbol in graduation ceremony | News Services | ECU
cards.access_notes: Appears in formal university ceremonies; attendance and guest policies vary by ceremony.
